title: General security requirements
summary: Ensure confidentiality integrity and availability of all ePHI created received maintained or transmitted; protect against reasonably anticipated threats, impermissible uses and disclosures; ensure workforce compliance.

title: Security management process (standard)
summary: Implement policies and procedures to prevent detect contain and correct security violations.

title: Risk analysis (required)
summary: Conduct an accurate and thorough assessment of risks and vulnerabilities to ePHI.
typical_evidence: Current enterprise-wide risk analysis covering all ePHI systems

title: Risk management (required)
summary: Implement security measures sufficient to reduce risks and vulnerabilities to a reasonable and appropriate level.
typical_evidence: Risk management plan; risk register with treatment status

title: Sanction policy (required)
summary: Apply appropriate sanctions against workforce members who fail to comply with security policies.
typical_evidence: Sanction policy; records of sanctions applied

title: Information system activity review (required)
summary: Regularly review records of system activity such as audit logs, access reports and security incident tracking.
typical_evidence: Log review procedure; review records; alert rules

title: Assigned security responsibility (required)
summary: Identify the security official responsible for developing and implementing security policies.

title: Workforce security (standard)
summary: Ensure workforce members have appropriate ePHI access and prevent access by those who should not have it.

title: Authorisation and/or supervision (addressable)
summary: Authorise or supervise workforce members who work with ePHI or where it may be accessed.
typical_evidence: Access authorisation records or documented alternative

title: Workforce clearance procedure (addressable)
summary: Determine that a workforce member's access to ePHI is appropriate.
typical_evidence: Background checks or clearance procedure, or documented alternative

title: Termination procedures (addressable)
summary: Terminate access to ePHI when employment ends or access is no longer appropriate.

title: Information access management (standard)
summary: Authorise access to ePHI consistent with the Privacy Rule.

title: Isolating health care clearinghouse functions (required)
summary: A clearinghouse that is part of a larger organisation protects its ePHI from the rest of the organisation.
typical_evidence: Only if the organisation includes a clearinghouse

title: Access authorisation (addressable)
summary: Policies and procedures for granting access to ePHI (e.g. workstation, program, process).

title: Access establishment and modification (addressable)
summary: Establish document review and modify a user's right of access.

title: Security awareness and training (standard)
summary: Implement a security awareness and training programme for all workforce members including management.

title: Security reminders (addressable)
summary: Periodic security updates.

title: Protection from malicious software (addressable)
summary: Procedures for guarding against, detecting and reporting malicious software.

title: Log-in monitoring (addressable)
summary: Procedures for monitoring log-in attempts and reporting discrepancies.
typical_evidence: Failed login alerting; IdP sign-in logs

title: Password management (addressable)
summary: Procedures for creating changing and safeguarding passwords.

title: Security incident procedures (standard)
summary: Implement policies and procedures to address security incidents.

title: Response and reporting (required)
summary: Identify and respond to suspected or known incidents; mitigate harmful effects; document incidents and outcomes.

title: Contingency plan (standard)
summary: Policies and procedures for responding to emergencies that damage systems containing ePHI.

title: Data backup plan (required)
summary: Create and maintain retrievable exact copies of ePHI.

title: Disaster recovery plan (required)
summary: Procedures to restore any loss of data.

title: Emergency mode operation plan (required)
summary: Procedures to continue critical business processes that protect ePHI while operating in emergency mode.

title: Testing and revision procedures (addressable)
summary: Periodically test and revise contingency plans.

title: Applications and data criticality analysis (addressable)
summary: Assess the relative criticality of applications and data supporting contingency plan components.

title: Evaluation (required)
summary: Perform periodic technical and non-technical evaluations of how well policies and procedures meet the rule, including after environmental or operational changes.
typical_evidence: Periodic security evaluation or internal audit report

title: Business associate contracts and other arrangements (standard)
summary: Permit a business associate to handle ePHI only with satisfactory assurances that it will safeguard it.

title: Written contract or other arrangement (required)
summary: Document the satisfactory assurances through a written contract meeting 164.314(a).

title: Facility access controls (standard)
summary: Limit physical access to electronic information systems and facilities while allowing authorised access.
typical_evidence: Facility access policy; cloud provider report (inherited)

title: Contingency operations (addressable)
summary: Procedures allowing facility access to support data restoration under the DR and emergency mode plans.

title: Facility security plan (addressable)
summary: Safeguard the facility and equipment from unauthorised physical access, tampering and theft.
typical_evidence: Facility security plan or inherited provider controls

title: Access control and validation procedures (addressable)
summary: Control and validate a person's access to facilities by role, including visitor control.

title: Maintenance records (addressable)
summary: Document repairs and modifications to physical security components.

title: Workstation use (required)
summary: Specify proper functions, the manner of use and the physical surroundings of workstations accessing ePHI.

title: Workstation security (required)
summary: Implement physical safeguards for all workstations that access ePHI to restrict access to authorised users.
typical_evidence: MDM report (encryption; screen lock); remote work policy

title: Device and media controls (standard)
summary: Govern receipt and removal of hardware and media containing ePHI.

title: Disposal (required)
summary: Address final disposal of ePHI and the hardware or media on which it is stored.

title: Media re-use (required)
summary: Remove ePHI from media before re-use.

title: Accountability (addressable)
summary: Record movements of hardware and media and the person responsible.

title: Data backup and storage (addressable)
summary: Create a retrievable exact copy of ePHI before moving equipment.

title: Access control (standard)
summary: Technical policies and procedures allowing access only to authorised persons or software.

title: Unique user identification (required)
summary: Assign a unique name or number to identify and track each user.
typical_evidence: IdP user export showing no shared accounts

title: Emergency access procedure (required)
summary: Procedures for obtaining necessary ePHI during an emergency.

title: Automatic logoff (addressable)
summary: Terminate an electronic session after a set time of inactivity.

title: Encryption and decryption (addressable)
summary: A mechanism to encrypt and decrypt ePHI at rest.

title: Audit controls (required)
summary: Mechanisms that record and examine activity in systems containing ePHI.

title: Integrity (standard)
summary: Protect ePHI from improper alteration or destruction.

title: Mechanism to authenticate ePHI (addressable)
summary: Corroborate that ePHI has not been altered or destroyed in an unauthorised manner.

title: Person or entity authentication (required)
summary: Verify that a person or entity seeking access to ePHI is who they claim to be.

title: Transmission security (standard)
summary: Guard against unauthorised access to ePHI transmitted over networks.

title: Integrity controls (addressable)
summary: Ensure transmitted ePHI is not improperly modified without detection.

title: Encryption (addressable)
summary: Encrypt ePHI in transit whenever deemed appropriate.
typical_evidence: TLS scan; encryption in transit policy

title: Business associate contracts (standard)
summary: BA contracts require the BA to comply with the Security Rule, ensure subcontractors agree to the same and report security incidents including breaches.

title: Requirements for group health plans (standard)
summary: Plan documents require the plan sponsor to safeguard ePHI.

title: Policies and procedures (standard)
summary: Implement reasonable and appropriate policies and procedures to comply with the rule.

title: Documentation (standard)
summary: Maintain written records of policies, procedures, actions, activities and assessments.

title: Time limit (required)
summary: Retain documentation for six years from creation or last effective date.

title: Availability (required)
summary: Make documentation available to those responsible for implementing the procedures.

title: Updates (required)
summary: Review documentation periodically and update it as needed.

title: Breach determination and risk assessment
summary: Treat any impermissible use or disclosure of unsecured PHI as a breach unless a documented four-factor risk assessment shows a low probability that the PHI was compromised (nature and extent of PHI, who received it, whether it was actually acquired or viewed, extent of mitigation).
typical_evidence: Breach assessment procedure with the four factors; completed assessments for incidents in the period

title: Notification to individuals (covered entities)
summary: Covered entities notify each affected individual without unreasonable delay and no later than 60 calendar days after discovery, by first-class mail or email if agreed, with the required content.
typical_evidence: Only for covered entities: notification templates; notification records

title: Notification to the media (covered entities)
summary: Covered entities notify prominent media outlets when a breach affects more than 500 residents of a State or jurisdiction.
typical_evidence: Only for covered entities: media notice procedure

title: Notification to the Secretary (covered entities)
summary: Covered entities notify HHS at the same time as individuals for breaches affecting 500 or more people; smaller breaches are logged and reported within 60 days of the end of the calendar year.
typical_evidence: Only for covered entities: HHS breach log and submissions

title: Notification by a business associate
summary: Business associates notify the covered entity of a breach of unsecured PHI without unreasonable delay and no later than 60 calendar days after discovery, identifying each affected individual where possible and giving the information the covered entity needs for its notices.
typical_evidence: Only for business associates: BAA breach notification clause; incident procedure step to notify covered entities; notification records

title: Law enforcement delay
summary: Delay notification when a law enforcement official states that it would impede a criminal investigation or damage national security.
typical_evidence: Procedure for documenting law enforcement delay requests

title: Burden of proof
summary: Covered entities and business associates must be able to show that all required notifications were made, or that an incident was not a breach.
typical_evidence: Breach register with assessments and notification evidence
